Windsor.ai is a global team of data engineers and analysts who strive to make data integration effortless and insights easy to extract to everyone. We help businesses of all sizes connect their marketing and sales data, automate reporting, and measure what drives the greatest impact.

My entrepreneurial journey began in 2003. I launched Scandinavia’s first Voice over Internet Protocol company, which taught me the excitement of building solutions that truly help businesses grow. I wanted to recreate that feeling by tackling one of the biggest challenges I’d seen in my career: integrating data and turning it into actionable insights.

This led me to realize how deep the connection with the previous experience was and find a new passion in building data-driven software that enables businesses to make better decisions working with startups in a variety of fields, from social media marketing optimization to the US healthcare industry.

My name is Matthias. To build, to move fast and to be around talented people is what I enjoy the most. That’s what Windsor.ai is all about. Prior to Windsor.ai I spent more than a decade setting up and growing software companies in Asia and Europe.

is the second-largest and most northerly of Japan's four main islands. It is separated from Aomori Prefecture on the Honshu mainland by the Tsugaru Strait (and connected by the Seikan Tunnel railway).

Hokkaido is the largest prefecture in Japan, forming its own 'region'. Unlike most other prefectures, it is usually referred to simply as 'Hokkaido', rather than 'Hokkaido Prefecture'. Sapporo City is the capital of Hokkaido and is famous for, among other things, the annual Sapporo Snow Festival held in February.

With a colder climate than most of Japan, Hokkaido enjoys some of the most consistent snowfall and conditions in the country. There are more ski areas in Hokkaido than in any other prefecture in Japan, and they are scattered throughout the mountains of the large island.

Hokkaido is home to some of Japan's most famous ski areas. The ski areas in Niseko and Kutchan in the west, and Furano in the central region, have long been popular with Japanese skiers. In recent years, those ski resorts, along with several others, have gained a worldwide reputation and now attract a significant number of overseas visitors.

A Day in Windsor, on the Outskirts of London 🇬🇧

I took a casual day trip to Windsor, located about 40 minutes to an hour from London by train. Windsor is famous for Windsor Castle, which is also one of the official residences of the British Royal Family.

I think the route from Paddington Station to Windsor is the most common, but I traveled from Waterloo on the Southwestern Railway. The station I arrived at is different from the one from Paddington, and it's about a 5-minute walk to the center of Windsor.

The station you arrive at if you visit from Paddington. This side has more tourists, the area around the station is more lively, and the buildings are historic and beautiful. You definitely get more excited arriving at this station.
Windsor Castle and The Long Walk
I went to Windsor Castle, a place Queen Elizabeth II particularly loved to stay, and also her burial site after she passed away in 2022.
The entrance fee was an exorbitant £35, so I didn't go inside and just looked from the outside. St. George's Chapel, where royal weddings are held, and the Changing of the Guard are famous here 💂
